I have formed this personal definition over the last few years. To me, art should

  • be unique, original and irreplaceable.
  • require exceptional talent, be it innate or taught, and effort to be created.
  • be successful in pleasing and/or awing the senses of the viewer/listener/...
  • be relevant to the society and their culture, politics, philosophy, religion, ...

It does not have to carry a message from the author. I know that that goes against the more popular understanding of art, but to me a work of art can stand on itself without deeper philosophical meaning.

All of this should of course be place in the context of the age it was created in. Take for example the art of sculpture. It has evolved rapidly over the Hellenistic and Roman ages, their statues far more beautiful than the Etruscan, but the fact that preceding works seem easy, maybe even trivial to make in later ages/nowadays does not mean that they should not be considered art anymore. They have earned their status in history and should be kept there.
